mechanism_narrative: The sharp one-week rebound in WORKPLACES from -27.9 to -11.0 signals a return of commuting and office-adjacent routines that raises weekday retail footfall over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose from -27.9 at t-1w to -11.0 at t-0w
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES continues above -11.0 yet mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than -11.475.

mechanism_narrative: Residential mobility declines from 6.7 to 5.6, indicating that fewer people are staying home, which releases household demand into out-of-home retail and recreation over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell from 6.7 at t-2w to 5.6 at t-0w
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL continues to fall below 5.6 but mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days remains below its prior 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT remains below -35 for two consecutive weeks (t-2w -36.6, t-1w -36.7), indicating persistent transit avoidance that limits access to dense retail districts and suppresses RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT weekly mean < -35 for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT was -36.6 at t-2w and -36.7 at t-1w
failure_condition: If TRANSIT stays below -35 for two more weeks but mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than -11.475.

mechanism_narrative: The positive RETAIL_REC effect of the WORKPLACES rebound depends on RESIDENTIAL easing: when WORKPLACES rises by more than 10 points week-on-week while RESIDENTIAL is at or below 6.0, retail footfall rises over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises >10 points week-on-week and RESIDENTIAL <= 6.0
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose from -27.9 to -11.0 while RESIDENTIAL fell from 6.4 to 5.6
failure_condition: If the joint condition holds but mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is not above -11.475.

mechanism_narrative: Under tightening restrictions, elevated RESIDENTIAL above 5.0 together with TRANSIT below -30 keeps discretionary trips suppressed, so RETAIL_REC declines over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL is 5.6 and TRANSIT is -33.7 at t-0w
failure_condition: If the tightening-restrictions regime persists with RESIDENTIAL >5.0 and TRANSIT <-30, yet mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than -11.475.

mechanism_narrative: The prior-week PARKS spike to 16.1 followed by a fall to 0.9 marks a seasonal shift from outdoor to indoor activity, which redirects recreation spending toward retail and lifts RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls >10 points from prior week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell from 16.1 at t-1w to 0.9 at t-0w
failure_condition: If PARKS remains near 0.9 or falls further while mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than -11.475.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM near baseline (-0.3) while RETAIL_REC is deeply negative (-12.3) shows households are limiting trips to essentials; this trip consolidation persists and keeps discretionary retail below its prior mean over the next week.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM is -0.3 and RETAIL_REC is -12.3 at t-0w
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM remains near zero while mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than -11.475.

mechanism_narrative: The simultaneous recovery in TRANSIT from -36.7 to -33.7 and WORKPLACES from -27.9 to -11.0 indicates policy easing that reopens retail corridors, producing higher RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises >2 points week-on-week and WORKPLACES rises >10 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT rose from -36.7 to -33.7 and WORKPLACES rose from -27.9 to -11.0
failure_condition: If both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES rise further but mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than -11.475.
